what: Grid, decision rule and shape prediction for the per-unit dB relative-term sweep (#782), committed BEFORE any point is measured. The instrument is tools/probes/rate_tol_sweep.py --unit db, committed in the same change and run only afterwards; its refusal on an uncommitted or dirty plan is the temporal proof, exactly as for the scalar sweep (#775) whose refusal this instrument already carries.
parameter: RATE_TOL_REL_DB in model/discrimination_features.py: the dB family's relative term, one of the five per-unit scalars the pre-#782 scalar RATE_TOL_REL split into. The comparison stays max(rel * peak, RATE_TOL_ABS[unit]); only the dB term moves, through rate_tolerance's per-unit dict override, which merges the override over the shipped values so the other four terms are held by construction rather than by promise. 147 of the 191 columns are dB, and #775's committed limits name this dial as the repair for the defect its narrowing exposed: a relative term on an offset scale licenses a bin by its distance from 0 dB, which for dB columns is backwards.
range_basis: 0.02 is the value the dB term carries until this change (every unit's term is 0.02 since #775). It is on the grid so the record prices the CHANGE and not only the dial, the same reason -1 is on fold-interpolator's grid and 0 is on dphase-ar1-floor's.

0.12 is the scalar that shipped until #775, under which the 7.0 dB null movement at 440 Hz sat hidden. It prices the top of the range and is the value #775's own committed scalar sweep measured panel_red = 0 at -- though with all five units moving, which this sweep holds fixed.

0.00625 = RATE_TOL_ABS['db'] / 80 dB. cqt_features and multiscale_features clamp at floor_db = -80.0, so 80 dB is the largest magnitude a dB column can carry and 0.00625 * 80 = 0.5 = the dB floor exactly: at this value and below it the relative term adds no licence anywhere in the dB family and the dial is inert. It is the arithmetic endpoint of 'the dB term cannot bind', paired with 0.0 which removes the term outright.

0.057 sits above the committed RATE_KNOWN_RED bounds of the two smaller null families -- cqt4064Hz 4.07/80 = 0.0509 and cqt2874Hz 4.43/80 = 0.0554 -- so it is the decision row for 'the smaller nulls pass'.
0.09 sits above the worst committed cqt3225Hz bound, 7.00/80 = 0.0875, with 2.9 % of margin. It is the decision row for 'every quarantined cqt null passes'.

0.1 is the headroom row: 14 % above the worst committed bound, the ship candidate if the 2.9 % margin at 0.09 is judged too thin against cross-version noise in the gaps. The choice between 0.09 and 0.1 is exactly the trade the sweep prices: both retire the same ten entries, and the objective says what the extra licence costs the control's sight.
held_fixed: the other four relative terms -- RATE_TOL_REL_PPM, RATE_TOL_REL_MS, RATE_TOL_REL_COUNT and RATE_TOL_REL_RATIO at their shipped 0.02, held by the override's merge over the shipped dict, not by promise; RATE_TOL_ABS's five absolute floors; FOLD_SINC_TAPS at its shipped 16 for the cost panel and at -1 for the benefit panel; and the stimulus panel itself: tools/probes/fold_rate_sweep.py's 44 values of f0 in both resampling directions, plus the two control shapes RATE_PANEL carries (0.1 % jitter, band-limited square) at both build rates.
objective: caught -- the number of (panel entry, column) pairs the rate-independence comparison turns red on the INTEGER FOLD that shipped before #767 (taps=-1), over the wide panel, through rate_tolerance itself with the dB term overridden. Higher is better: it is how much real 44.1k<->48k dependence the control can see. The other four relative terms are held at their shipped 0.02 by the override's merge, so every move in caught between two grid points is attributable to the dB term alone; #775's record (rate-tol-rel.json) remains the pricing of the all-units scalar. jit.* columns are excluded on any entry where dominant_period disagrees between the two rates by more than 5 % (#774), exactly as in #775's sweep.
constraint: cost -- the same count on the SHIPPED fold, split by unit (cost_by_unit), plus the ELEVEN-ENTRY RATE_PANEL count read through _rate_gaps itself (shipped_panel). The wide-panel cost is the price of a clean panel going red; the shipped panel is the count that decides whether RATE_KNOWN_RED entries retire, because RATE_PANEL is what test_extra_features_are_rate_independent runs. A dB-family tightening that never shows on the shipped panel would be a wide-panel-only artefact.

decision_rule.why: the objective is an INTEGER COUNT of (entry, column) pairs. Two counts are equal or they are not; there is no 'within' for a count, so the rule has to be exact equality. The wide panel is at most 92 entries x 191 columns = 17572 pairs, so any relative tolerance below 1/17572 = 5.7e-5 is exact equality by construction, and 1e-5 is below that with a factor of 5.7 to spare -- the same derivation #775's record states, from the objective's own granularity and the panel's size, both known before the sweep ran.

prediction.basis: Derived from the max() arithmetic, the module's own magnitude ceilings, and #775's committed artefact -- none of which is a point on this sweep. (a) MONOTONE: raising the dB term can only raise a dB pair's tolerance, so caught and caught_db are non-increasing in the dial and every group is an interval; the other four units' counts cannot move at all, which the instrument's per-unit monotone test asserts. (b) [0.0, 0.00625] is ONE group: for every dB pair peak <= 80 (the floor_db clamp), rel * peak <= 0.5 = RATE_TOL_ABS['db'], so the tolerance equals the floor for every dB column at both points -- the dial is inert below 0.00625, the same argument #775's scalar prediction made for the whole vector, now exact because the dB family is the only family that moves. (c) 0.02 separates: #775's committed cost-by-unit table shows dB pairs with clean-fold crossings throughout (0.00625, 0.02] -- 15 pairs in (0.00625, 0.0146] and 11 in (0.0146, 0.02] -- and the integer fold's dB gaps on the same stimuli are at least as large (its caught exceeds the clean cost at every committed value), so the injected fold has crossings there too and caught at 0.00625 exceeds caught at 0.02. (d) 0.057, 0.09, 0.1, 0.12 each separate: the committed cost-by-unit counts (95 dB clean-fold pairs red at 0.02 falling to 4 at 0.12) mean 91 dB pairs have crossings spread over (0.02, 0.12], and #775's committed reach table names cqt null crossings at 0.081-0.0895 -- every interval except possibly (0.09, 0.1] has a crossing visible above the reach table's top-24 cut; for (0.09, 0.1] the count argument carries it (48 dB pairs in (0.06, 0.12] against only ~8 visible in the cut, so the rest populate the intervals below, including this one), and the integer fold shifts crossings up rather than down. Verdict MIXED, 6 groups over 7 points.

what_would_falsify_it: caught differing between 0.0 and 0.00625 refutes (b): it would take a dB pair with peak above 80 dB, which the floor_db clamp forbids -- so the real suspects would be an override leaking into a non-dB unit or a non-dB column mis-keyed as dB by _unit_of.

A plateau spanning (0.057, 0.09] or (0.09, 0.1] refutes (d)'s count argument: the 48 dB pairs with committed clean-fold crossings in (0.06, 0.12] would have to cluster elsewhere than the interval, which is possible and would be recorded -- the ship decision would then rest on the shipped-panel table rather than on the objective's staircase.

The shipped panel going empty at 0.09 would falsify the prediction's reading of the msd10-25ms 880 Hz entry: its committed bound (gap 0.89) retires only if its crossing 0.89/peak lands at or under 0.09, and the basis assumes the band's peak is a few dB, making the crossing ~0.2 or more. If it retires at 0.09, the peak estimate was wrong and the entry retires anyway -- a correction to the basis, recorded, not a change of verdict.

cost_ratio or caught_ratio moving between any two grid points would refute (a)'s scope claim: the dB override must not touch the ratio family, and the instrument's own tests assert it on hand-built pairs.
